sentences.text: This petition under Section 166 MV Act is filed seeking compensation of .7,00,000/ for the injuries sustained by the Petitioner in a road traffic accident.

2. It is stated that on 22092021 about 7.35 a.m., the Petitioner was riding his motorbike near S.Mens Saloon, M.S.Complex, No.83/1, Muddinapalya Main road, Bengaluru, at that time, the driver of Bolero Jeep bearing No.KA02G1002 (hereinafter called as offending vehicle) drove the same with high speed, took reverse without any signal in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the Petitioner's motorbike.
Due to the accident, Petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
He was immediately taken to London Care Hospital, after first aid he was shifted to Neighborhood hospital, Bengaluru, wherein he has taken treatment as an inpatient and underwent surgery.
Due to the accidental injuries, he is suffering from permanent disability and unable to lead normal life as earlier.
It is claimed that Petitioner has spent .2,00,000/ for treatment, medicines, conveyance and other charges.

At the time of accident, Petitioner was aged 51 years, he was working as a Junior Training Officer at Vokkaligara Sangha, ITI College, Bengaluru and earning a sum of .50,000/
p.m.
Due to accidental injuries he was unable to attend his job for 26 days and sustained loss of Rs.30,000/.
As the accident was caused due to negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle, it is requested to award compensation from the Respondent No.1 insured and Respondent No.2 Insurer.
3. In response to the petition notice, the Respondent No.2 has appeared before the court through its counsel and filed the objection.
The Respondent No.1 has not appeared before the court and he was placed exparte.
4. The Respondent No.2 has filed his objection by contending that the petitioner has failed to make the owner and insurer of the motorbike as parties in the case who are necessary parties.
It has contended that the accident has not occurred due to negligence of driver of offending vehicle.

On the other hand, it has contended that the rider of motorcycle i.e. Petitioner was rash and negligent in riding his vehicle and he was not holding valid DL, insurance and due to his negligence the accident occurred.
Further, the Petitioner has continued his work and as such, he is not entitle any compensation.
Further it has contended that the offending vehicle belongs to the 1st Respondent and it was insured with the Respondent No.2 and policy was valid from 13 072021 to 1207 2022.
The compensation claimed by the Petitioner is exorbitant.
For all these reasons, this Respondent prayed for dismissal of the petition.
5. On the basis of the above pleadings, the following Issues were framed :

-
1. Whether the Petitioner proves that he sustained injuries when he was riding in his motorcycle bearing No.KA04EG3664 on 2209 2021 opposite S Mens Saloon,

2 No.83/1, M.S.Complex, Muddinapalya Main Road, Bengaluru, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of Bolero Jeep bearing No.KA02G 1002?
2.

6. In order to prove the claim, the Petitioner examined himself as PW.1 and doctor is examined as PW2 and got marked the documents as per Ex.P.1 to P.18 respectively.
7. The Respondent No.2 has not adduced any oral and documentary evidence.
8. I have heard the counsel on both sides and have perused the material on record.

9. My findings to the above issues are as under:
Issue No.1: In the Affirmative.
Issue No.2: Partly in affirmative.

Issue No.3: As per the final order, for the following:
R E A S O N S 10.
ISSUE NO.1:
In order to prove his claim, Petitioner relied on the police and medical records.
PW1 is the injured and the direct witness to the incident.

He has deposed that on 22092021 about 7.35 a.m., hewas riding his motorbike near S.Mens Saloon, M.S.Complex, No.83/1,
Muddinapalya Main road, Bengaluru, at that time, the driver of Bolero Jeep bearing No.KA02G 1002 drove the same with high speed, took reverse without any signal in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to his motorbike.
Due to the accident, he fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
It is stated that the accident was solely due to rash and negligent act of the driver of the offending vehicle.

11. In support of his claim he has produced copy of FIR at Ex.P.1, complaint at Ex.P.2, spot mahazar at Ex.P.3, spot sketch at Ex.P.4, IMV report at Ex.P.5 & 6, Wound certificate at Ex.P.7 and charge sheet at Ex.P.8.
As per wound certificate he has sustained fracture of both left radius and ulna bone.
12. It is the contention of the Respondent  Insurance Company that it was the negligence of Petitioner himself who was riding the motorcycle in a rash and negligent manner.
It is contended that the Petitioner was riding the motorcycle without DL and insurance and caused the accident.
PW.1 has denied all the suggestions during the cross examination.
As he was admitted in the hospital, he has given first information statement to the police after discharge from the hospital.
13. On perusal of wound certificate and discharge summary it is clear that on the date of accident itself it is mentioned that it was the history of RTA between twowheeler and four wheeler.
The hospital authorities must have informed the police about the admission of the injured in the hospital.
Even it was the duty of the police they have not registered FIR immediately.

It is obvious Nagaraju N.J vs The Deputy Commissioner Of Police on 15 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/199756600/

sentences.text: that the injured was in the hospital and the complaint was delayed.
It cannot be denied that the accident was occurred between two wheeler and Bolero vehicle.

After complete investigation police have filed chargesheet against both the driver of the offending vehicle and rider motorcycle i.e.,
petitioner and it appears that it is challenged by the Petitioner before the Hon'ble High Court in Cr.petition No.6215/2022 dated 18032024, which resulted in quashing of the proceedings against the petitioner.
14. Now the criminal case pending against the driver of offending vehicle alone.
It appears that it was the negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle in causing the accident.
Petitioner has proved that it was the negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle in causing the accident due to which he sustained severe injuries.
For all these reasons, I have answered the Issue No.1 in the Affirmative.
15. ISSUE NO.2 :
The Petitioner states that he was aged about 51 years as on the date of accident.
Due to the accident he has sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately he was taken to London care hospital, after first aid he was shifted to Neighbourhood hospital, wherein, he was treated as an inpatient.
After discharge from the hospital he has taken followup treatment.

He has stated that at the time of accident, he was work as a Junior Training Officer at Vokkaligara Sangha, ITI College,
Bengaluru and earning a sum of .50,000/ p.m.
Due to the accidental injuries he was unable to attend his job for 26 days and suffered loss to the tune of Rs.30,000/.
He has lost his normal life as earlier and suffering huge loss of income.

16. PW2 Dr. Girish S, Orthopedic surgeon at Neighbourhoood hospital, Bengaluru, has deposed that the Petitioner has sustained injuries in a RTA and treated in their hospital and stated that at casualty petitioner was immobilized with splint and started with IV fluids and analgesics, he was stabilized and physician opinion taken and he was taken for ORIF LCP/DCP under GA of both bones on the same day; after discharge, he has attended followup treatment regularly.
PW2 has examined the Petitioner clinically and taken Xrays while assessing disability on 13032024.
He found that Petitioner complains of mild pain while doing heavy work, minimal discomfort in rotational activities.
Xray showed united fracture with implants in situ.
On examination he has assessed the total body permanent disability at 7%.
17. PW2 in his crossexamination has stated that he has examined the Petitioner 2 3 times after discharge.
He denied that the disability will reduce after removal of implants.
He has admitted that he does not have any difficulties in driving a vehicle or to do his daytoday normal activities.

18. Though petitioner has examined the doctor, he has admitted in his cross examination that now he is getting salary of Rs.60,000/ p.m. and not produced any documents to show his occupation and income.
It shows that he has continued his job and there is no loss of income due to accidental injuries.
Hence, he is not entitled for compensation under the head of loss of future earnings.
So also, the petitioner has stated that he has not attended his work for 26 days, but he has not produced any documents in this regard.
More over he has not produced any proof for his occupation and income.
Hence, he is also not entitled for loss of income during treatment period.

sentences.text: Pain and sufferings:

So far as the compensation under nonpecuniary damages are concerned,
considering the fact that the Petitioner has suffered fracture of both of left radius and ulna bone and was inpatient for a period of 3 days which caused him to immeasurable mental agony and pain, I am of the opinion that an amount of .40,000/ would be just and fair compensation under the head pain and sufferings.
20. Loss of amenities of life:
For loss of amenities of life undoubtedly Petitioner is sure to suffer in his day today activities and face hardships.
Hence, Petitioner is awarded .20,000/ under loss of amenities of life.
21. Medical expenses:

Under the pecuniary damages, expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization and medicines, the Petitioner has produced a pharmacy bill at Ex.P.12 for Rs.888/ and IP bill at Ex.P.13 amounting to 75,000/.
There is no crossexamination regarding his medical expenses.

Considering the genuineness of medical bills, Petitioner is awarded compensation of 75,888/
towards Medical Expenses.
22. Future medical expenses:
PW.2doctor has stated that Petitioner is required to undergo surgery for removal of implant, which may costs 50,000/ to 60,000/.
In support of his version PW2 has not produced any estimation.

In the absence of clear estimation of the future medical expenses,
it would be proper to award 20,000/ towards Future medical expenses.
23. Conveyance, food, nourishment and attendant charges:
Ex.P.9Discharge summary shows that Petitioner was treated as an inpatient at Neighbourhood hospital, Bengaluru from 22092021 to 24092021 i.e, for a period of 3 days.

By considering the discharge summary and other records, it is just and reasonable to award compensation of 3,000/ under the head of conveyance, food,
nourishment and attendant charges.

24. Thus the compensation awarded under the various heads are as under:
Sl. Nature of Compensation Amount No.
1. Pain and Sufferings . 40,000/
2. Loss of amenities .

3. Medical expenses . 75,888/
4.
Future medical expenses .

20,000/
5. Conveyance, Food, . 3,000/ Nourishment & Attendant charges Total .
1,58,888/

The Respondent No.1 insured and RC owner and Respondent No.2 insurer are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioner.

26. ISSUE NO.3 :

In view of the above discussion, reasons stated and findings given to Issue Nos. 1 & 2, I proceed to pass the following:
O R D E R Claim Petition filed under Sec.166 of M.V.Act is allowed in part with cost.
 Petitioner is awarded  compensation of .1,58,888/
together with interest @ 6% p.a. (Except future medical expenses) from the date of petition till the date of deposit with the Tribunal.
Respondent No.2 shall pay the aforesaid amount within two months from the date of this order.
On deposit, the entire amount along with interest shall be released in favour of the Petitioner through Epayment on proper identification and verification.

Advocate's fee is fixed at  .1,000/.
 Draw award accordingly.
